gaps.sentence: He is very ___ to criticism and takes it personally.
gaps.hint: easily affected or hurt; pattern: ___ to
gaps.explanation: 'Sensitive to something' means easily affected or upset by it; 'sensible' means showing good judgement.

gaps.sentence: Please state your ___ on the application form.
gaps.hint: the formal word for your type of work, used on forms
gaps.explanation: 'Occupation' is the formal word for a person's job or profession, typically used on official forms.

gaps.sentence: Many people fell asleep ___ the lecture.
gaps.hint: within the period of an event
gaps.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun (the lecture) and means within that time; 'while' needs a clause with a verb.

gaps.sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
gaps.hint: for a group of more than two
gaps.explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.
'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.
